body:
This exception is similar to gnu-javamail-exception but @jlovejoy thinks the differences are justifiable for separate id.
Also note that some use usage says "if you link a sane-airscan library" while others "if you link a SANE library".

Exception text for reference:

> As a special exception, the authors of sane-airscan give permission for
> additional uses of the libraries contained in this release of sane-airscan.
> 
> The exception is that, if you link a sane-airscan library with other files
> to produce an executable, this does not by itself cause the
> resulting executable to be covered by the GNU General Public
> License.  Your use of that executable is in no way restricted on
> account of linking the sane-airscan library code into it.
> 
> This exception does not, however, invalidate any other reasons why
> the executable file might be covered by the GNU General Public
> License.
> 
> If you submit changes to sane-airscan to the maintainers to be included in
> a subsequent release, you agree by submitting the changes that
> those changes may be distributed with this exception intact.
> 
> If you write modifications of your own for sane-airscan, it is your choice
> whether to permit this exception to apply to your modifications.
> If you do not wish that, delete this exception notice.

+1 to add this as a separate license exception. 

A number of exceptions (the javamail one, also GNAT-exception and Fawkes-Runtime-exception) contain portions of language that are similar, but I don't see any that would be a substantive match for this one. In particular the requirement that submitting changes to the maintainers means that those changes may be distributed with this exception intact is something I don't recall seeing in other exceptions.

I think this meets the [Exception Inclusion Principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md#license-exceptions):

* not a stand-alone license
* grants an exception to a condition / grants an additional permission
* doesn't impose additional restrictions
  - ...other than arguably the "you agree by submitting the changes," but I view that more as a reference to contribution requirements more than an obligation on downstream redistribution / modification
* actual substantial use via inclusion in Fedora and also SANE's widespread use independently of Fedora

`SANE-exception` as the ID and "SANE Exception" for the name look good to me.
